## Findings

**1. "The representation", line 72 (pasted sentence, against itself and against the pasted Baked cells of lines 39 to 44).** The sentence says baking changes no piece's outline and then that the outline is toasted dark, and says no size changes while the grid's baking moves shrink the mushroom, curl the worm and soften the cheese's corners without saying the piece comes back. Replace the last sentence of the paragraph ("Baking changes no piece's size, outline or colour: ... as it lands.") with:

`Baking changes no piece's size, shape or fill colour: each kind does its baking move from the grid once as the pizza slides out, springs back to the size and shape it had, and then lies still on a browned base with only the line of its outline toasted dark, so a baked piece still pairs by eye with its drawn piece on the card, and a piece tapped onto a baked pizza takes the toasted outline as it lands.`

**2. "The object-by-action grid", line 39 fourth cell and line 41 sixth cell (ruling 8).** Line 35 says every cell looks and sounds different; the olive fed by hand names a motion and no sound, and the pepper's "puff" is used in this sheet for a look (line 43 "a flump and a small puff", line 157 gives the puff a shape only), so that cell names no sound either. Replace the two rows with:

`| Pepper | A snappy tick as it lands; it skids a little and stops | Blisters with a hiss | One puff of flame for each extra pepper, each with a whoomph | The monster fans its open mouth at the pepper tub, one rumble for each missing, each ending in a dry pant | It gulps, its cheeks glow and one spark pops out of an ear |`

`| Olive | A hollow pop; it rolls a finger-width and stops | Glistens and one goes "tok" | One eye rolls right round for each extra, with a rattle like a marble in a cup | It peers through an olive-sized ring of its fingers at the tub, one rumble for each missing, each ending in a hollow hoot | It swallows it whole with a plunk, like a pebble dropped down a well, and the lump travels visibly down to its belly |`

(Checked and not a fault: the "too few" column shares the rumble and differs in each ending, which ruling 8 allows.)

"The records", us-ca, line 192 (ruling 10).** "That lane works with numerals and sums" speaks for a whole lane, and `grade-1` returns four lanes; its mathematics lane also holds records on length, shapes and sorting. Replace the sentence "Ages 6 and 7 return `grade-1`, and the game is designed from no grade 1 record: that lane works with numerals and sums, which this game does not show." with:

``Ages 6 and 7 return `grade-1`, and the game is designed from no grade 1 record, which is the game's own choice: it shows no numerals and no sums.``

**4. "The records", us-ca 2.1, line 209 (ruling 9).** That record's Limits says no length of time is given, but is silent on a number of steps, so the steps are "Not in Limits", not "Left open by Limits". Replace the last sentence "Left open by Limits: the length of time and the number of steps, so a job of three steps is the game's own choice." with:

`Left open by Limits: the length of time, of which it gives no more than short and longer. Not in Limits: the number of steps; a job of three steps is the game's own choice.`

**5. "The claim", line 243, with us-ca lines 196, 200 and 205 (ruling 9).** The claim names whole six records of which the sheet takes a part: 1.2 (the number words are not asked), 1.6 (the later-age statement only, and no telling), K.CC.5 (line 202 says counting out is not taken), K.CC.6 (no telling), 2.1 (line 209 says no adult support is given) and `nl rw/gb/2/03/fase1` (line 228 says ordering is not used). Lines 202, 209 and 228 already say beside the code what is not taken; lines 196, 200 and 205 do not.

Line 243, replace the paragraph with:

`Monster Pizza is designed from, in California, three foundations published by a state department for preschool and transitional kindergarten (mathematics 1.2 and 1.6, and approaches to learning 2.1, each in part), which are foundations and not standards, and two kindergarten content standards adopted by the State Board of Education (K.CC.5 and K.CC.6, both in part); and, in the Netherlands, guidance of the curriculum institute SLO, which is not law: one statement of its content card for peuters, which says what can be offered to children before school, and three of its goals for fase 1 (rw/gb/2/01/fase1, rw/gb/2/08/fase1 and, in part, rw/gb/2/03/fase1), which say what a school can offer and not what a child must know. All nine records are confirmed. From the California records the game takes counting a set one thing at a time, counting to find how many, and comparing two sets as more, fewer or as many, with sets of up to ten. Of 1.2 it takes one act and one note for each thing, and it asks for no number word. Of 1.6 it takes the later-age statement, and of 1.6 and K.CC.6 the comparing and not the telling of it, since the game has no words. Of K.CC.5 it takes counting to find how many and not counting out from a number that is told. Of 2.1 it takes the amount to act on and the job of several steps, without the adult support that both of its statements include. From the Dutch records it takes pairing one to one, counting to find how many, comparing two amounts and not putting amounts in order, and representing a pictured amount with objects, with sets of up to ten. Making the set from a picture is taken from the Dutch goal rw/gb/2/08/fase1 alone, and an order of one to three kinds worked through in a job of several steps from the California foundation 2.1 alone. It is designed from no California record for a seven-year-old or for making a set from a picture, and from no Dutch record for the steps of a job.`

Line 196, replace the line, keeping its two-space indent, with:

`  What the game takes: one tap, one piece and one note for each thing, so a child who counts aloud has one piece for each word. Not taken: the saying of the number words, which the game does not ask for and leaves to the child; the game itself says no number word.`

Line 200, replace the line, keeping its two-space indent, with:

`  Limits taken: two groups only, at both ages. The game's orders fall under the later-age statement, which applies from age 4: the comparison is made by counting, and the difference need not be plain to see. The earlier-age statement has sets that are plainly equal or plainly unequal, with counting optional, and an order that is one piece off is beyond it. Not taken: the child's telling of how the two sets compare, which the record has at both ages; the game has no words and takes the comparing only. Left open by Limits: the number range, which is the game's own choice of ten. How many more is not asked, and the game never asks it: a tasting plays the difference out, and the child is not asked to name it. An order of two or three kinds is several pairs of groups on one pizza, which is the game's own choice.`
